description: Banco oficial de micro-conversaciones guiadas para las rutas A1-C2 de Speaking. Cada tarjeta es un intercambio breve: una situacion (setup), el rol del alumno (you), la linea del interlocutor (app_line) y una respuesta modelo abierta (model_response). El alumno escucha la linea, responde hablando con sus palabras y tras la evaluacion se revela la respuesta modelo. Alineado con los can_do y el lexico de backend/curriculum/<level>.json.

items.setup: A new classmate introduces herself at the first lesson.
items.you: Say hello, give your name and say you are happy to meet her.
items.app_line: Hello! I am Sara. Nice to meet you.
items.model_response: Hello Sara, my name is Mark. Nice to meet you too.

items.setup: You meet a friend at a party and she asks about your day.
items.you: Say hello and tell her you are fine.
items.app_line: Hi Mark! How are you today?
items.model_response: Hi! I am fine, thank you. And you?

items.setup: Your teacher asks where you come from.
items.you: Say which country you are from and that you speak Spanish.
items.app_line: Tell me a little about you. Where are you from?
items.model_response: I am from Mexico. I speak Spanish.

items.setup: A colleague wants to know your family.
items.you: Say that you have one brother and one sister.
items.app_line: Do you have brothers or sisters?
items.model_response: Yes, I have one brother and one sister.

items.setup: Someone asks what you do at school.
items.you: Say that you are a student.
items.app_line: And what do you do? Are you a student?
items.model_response: Yes, I am a student. I study English.

items.setup: A friend asks where you live now.
items.you: Say that you live in a small flat in the city.
items.app_line: Where do you live now?
items.model_response: I live in a small flat in the city.

items.setup: A form asks about your age at a language school.
items.you: Tell the receptionist how old you are.
items.app_line: Can I have your age, please?
items.model_response: I am twenty-six years old.

items.setup: A new friend wants your telephone number.
items.you: Say you can give it and share the number.
items.app_line: Can you give me your phone number?
items.model_response: Yes, of course. My number is 555 12 34 56.

items.setup: Someone asks when your birthday is.
items.you: Say the month of your birthday.
items.app_line: When is your birthday?
items.model_response: My birthday is in March.

items.setup: The hotel receptionist asks for your name.
items.you: Say your name and spell it slowly.
items.app_line: What is your name, please?
items.model_response: My name is Laura. L-A-U-R-A.

items.setup: A classmate asks what languages you speak.
items.you: Say you speak Spanish and a little English.
items.app_line: What languages do you speak?
items.model_response: I speak Spanish and a little English.

items.setup: A friend asks what your favourite colour is.
items.you: Answer and ask about her favourite colour.
items.app_line: What is your favourite colour?
items.model_response: My favourite colour is blue. What about you?

items.setup: Your host family asks what time you get up.
items.you: Say what time you get up in the morning.
items.app_line: What time do you get up?
items.model_response: I get up at seven in the morning.

items.setup: A friend asks what you have for breakfast.
items.you: Say you have bread and coffee.
items.app_line: What do you have for breakfast?
items.model_response: I have bread and coffee for breakfast.

items.setup: Your flatmate asks how you go to work.
items.you: Say you go to work by bus.
items.app_line: How do you go to work?
items.model_response: I go to work by bus every day.

items.setup: A colleague asks what you do after work.
items.you: Say you watch TV at home.
items.app_line: What do you do after work?
items.model_response: After work I go home and watch TV.

items.setup: A friend asks what you do on Sundays.
items.you: Say you visit your family on Sundays.
items.app_line: What do you do on Sundays?
items.model_response: On Sundays I visit my family.

items.setup: Your teacher asks when you do your homework.
items.you: Say you do your homework in the evening.
items.app_line: When do you do your homework?
items.model_response: I do my homework in the evening.

items.setup: A waiter asks what you want to drink.
items.you: Order a glass of water, please.
items.app_line: What would you like to drink?
items.model_response: A glass of water, please.

items.setup: Your friend asks if you like tea.
items.you: Say no, you prefer coffee.
items.app_line: Do you like tea?
items.model_response: No, I do not like tea. I prefer coffee.

items.setup: A friend asks about your favourite food.
items.you: Say your favourite food is pizza.
items.app_line: What is your favourite food?
items.model_response: My favourite food is pizza.

items.setup: You are at a cafe and want to pay.
items.you: Ask for the bill, please.
items.app_line: Is everything OK with your order?
items.model_response: Yes, thank you. Can I have the bill, please?

items.setup: A friend asks if you like fruit.
items.you: Say yes, you eat an apple every day.
items.app_line: Do you like fruit?
items.model_response: Yes, I like fruit. I eat an apple every day.

items.setup: A waiter asks if you want dessert.
items.you: Say yes, you want an ice cream.
items.app_line: Do you want a dessert?
items.model_response: Yes, please. I want an ice cream.

items.setup: A friend asks if you live with your family.
items.you: Say yes, you live with your parents.
items.app_line: Do you live with your family?
items.model_response: Yes, I live with my parents.

items.setup: Someone asks about your grandmother.
items.you: Say she is seventy years old.
items.app_line: How old is your grandmother?
items.model_response: My grandmother is seventy years old.

items.setup: A classmate asks if you have pets.
items.you: Say you have a dog called Max.
items.app_line: Do you have any pets?
items.model_response: Yes, I have a dog. His name is Max.

items.setup: Your new neighbour asks about your house.
items.you: Say your house has three rooms.
items.app_line: How big is your house?
items.model_response: It is small. It has three rooms.

items.setup: A friend asks what your parents do.
items.you: Say your mother is a doctor.
items.app_line: What does your mother do?
items.model_response: My mother is a doctor. My father is a teacher.

items.setup: Someone asks if you have a brother.
items.you: Say no, but you have two sisters.
items.app_line: Is that your brother in the photo?
items.model_response: No, I do not have a brother. I have two sisters.

items.setup: A shop assistant asks if she can help you.
items.you: Say you want to buy a T-shirt.
items.app_line: Can I help you?
items.model_response: Yes, I want to buy a T-shirt.

items.setup: A shop assistant tells you the price.
items.you: Say thank you and ask where to pay.
items.app_line: That is fifteen euros.
items.model_response: OK, thank you. Where can I pay?

items.setup: A tourist asks where the station is.
items.you: Say it is next to the bank.
items.app_line: Excuse me, where is the station?
items.model_response: It is next to the bank.

items.setup: You are in a shoe shop and a size is too big.
items.you: Ask for a smaller size.
items.app_line: How is the size?
items.model_response: It is too big. Can I have a smaller size?

items.setup: A friend asks where the supermarket is.
items.you: Say it is near the park, on the left.
items.app_line: Do you know where the supermarket is?
items.model_response: Yes, it is near the park on the left.

items.setup: A cashier asks if you want a bag.
items.you: Say yes, please.
items.app_line: Do you want a bag?
items.model_response: Yes, please. Thank you.

items.setup: You arrive late to a class and the teacher looks at you.
items.you: Apologise and explain you missed the bus.
items.app_line: You are late again today.
items.model_response: I am sorry. I missed the bus this morning.

items.setup: Your phone rings during a meeting.
items.you: Apologise and turn it off.
items.app_line: Is that your phone? We are in the meeting.
items.model_response: Sorry, I forgot to turn it off. It will not happen again.

items.setup: Your friend invites you to dinner tonight.
items.you: Accept the invitation happily.
items.app_line: Would you like to come to dinner tonight?
items.model_response: Yes, I would love to. What time shall I come?

items.setup: Your friend asks for help moving house.
items.you: Agree and say when you are free.
items.app_line: Could you help me move house on Saturday?
items.model_response: Of course. I am free on Saturday morning.

items.setup: A waiter brings you the wrong dish.
items.you: Explain the problem politely and ask for the correct dish.
items.app_line: Here is your chicken with rice.
items.model_response: I am sorry, but I ordered fish, not chicken.

items.setup: Your neighbour complains about the music.
items.you: Apologise and say you will make it quieter.
items.app_line: Could you please turn the music down?
items.model_response: I am really sorry. I will turn it down now.

items.setup: Your friend wants to know if the shop is open now.
items.you: Say you do not know and suggest checking online.
items.app_line: Do you know if the supermarket is open now?
items.model_response: I am not sure. We can check online.

items.setup: Your boss asks you to work on Saturday.
items.you: Say you cannot because you have other plans.
items.app_line: Can you come to the office on Saturday?
items.model_response: I am sorry, I cannot. I already have plans.

items.setup: A friend asks about your last holiday.
items.you: Say you went to the beach and it was great.
items.app_line: Where did you go on your last holiday?
items.model_response: I went to the beach with my family. It was great.

items.setup: A colleague asks what you did at the weekend.
items.you: Say you watched a film and visited friends.
items.app_line: What did you do last weekend?
items.model_response: I watched a film and I visited some friends.

items.setup: Your friend asks if you have been to London.
items.you: Say yes, you went there two years ago.
items.app_line: Have you ever been to London?
items.model_response: Yes, I went there two years ago.

items.setup: A friend asks how your exams went.
items.you: Say they went well and you are happy.
items.app_line: How were your exams?
items.model_response: They went very well, thanks. I am really happy.

items.setup: Your teacher asks about your first day at school.
items.you: Say you were nervous but the people were nice.
items.app_line: Tell me about your first day at school.
items.model_response: I was a little nervous, but the people were very nice.

items.setup: A friend asks about the film you saw last night.
items.you: Say it was funny and recommend it.
items.app_line: How was the film last night?
items.model_response: It was really funny. You should watch it too.

items.setup: Your flatmate asks why you were late yesterday.
items.you: Say you woke up late because your alarm did not work.
items.app_line: Why were you late yesterday?
items.model_response: I woke up late because my alarm did not work.

items.setup: A classmate asks if you enjoyed the party.
items.you: Say yes, and mention the music was good.
items.app_line: Did you enjoy the party last night?
items.model_response: Yes, I loved it. The music was really good.

items.setup: You are at a train station ticket office.
items.you: Ask for a ticket to the city centre.
items.app_line: Good morning, how can I help you?
items.model_response: Hello, I would like a ticket to the city centre, please.

items.setup: You are on a bus and you are not sure about the stop.
items.you: Ask the driver to tell you when to get off.
items.app_line: Next stop, Central Avenue.
items.model_response: Excuse me, can you tell me when to get off for the museum?

items.setup: You arrive at a hotel without a reservation.
items.you: Ask if they have a free room for two nights.
items.app_line: Welcome to the Grand Hotel. How can I help?
items.model_response: Do you have a free room for two nights, please?

items.setup: A friend asks how long the journey takes.
items.you: Say it takes about two hours by car.
items.app_line: How long is the journey to the coast?
items.model_response: It takes about two hours by car.

items.setup: Your colleague asks how you usually travel to work.
items.you: Say you usually take the underground.
items.app_line: How do you usually get to work?
items.model_response: I usually take the underground, it is faster.

items.setup: A tourist asks you for directions to the square.
items.you: Say it is a ten-minute walk from here.
items.app_line: How far is the main square from here?
items.model_response: It is about a ten-minute walk from here.

items.setup: Your friend asks about your favourite place to visit.
items.you: Say you love the mountains and go there every summer.
items.app_line: Do you have a favourite place to visit?
items.model_response: Yes, I love the mountains. I go there every summer.

items.setup: The bus does not arrive and you are in a hurry.
items.you: Ask a stranger when the next bus comes.
items.app_line: Are you waiting for the number 12 bus too?
items.model_response: Yes. Do you know when the next one comes?

items.setup: You feel tired all the time and talk to a friend.
items.you: Say you feel tired and ask for advice.
items.app_line: You look really tired lately.
items.model_response: I feel tired all the time. What do you think I should do?

items.setup: A friend has a headache at work.
items.you: Suggest resting and drinking water.
items.app_line: I have a terrible headache.
items.model_response: You should rest for a while and drink some water.

items.setup: Your friend asks how you stay healthy.
items.you: Say you walk every day and sleep well.
items.app_line: How do you stay healthy?
items.model_response: I walk every day and I try to sleep well.

items.setup: You are at the doctor and she asks what is wrong.
items.you: Say you have a sore throat since yesterday.
items.app_line: What seems to be the problem?
items.model_response: I have a sore throat since yesterday.

items.setup: A friend says she feels stressed before exams.
items.you: Suggest doing sport to relax.
items.app_line: I feel so stressed about my exams.
items.model_response: Why do not you do some sport? It helps me relax.

items.setup: You want to start eating better.
items.you: Tell a friend you want to eat more vegetables.
items.app_line: Do you want to share a salad for lunch?
items.model_response: Good idea. I want to eat more vegetables this month.

items.setup: Your flatmate cannot sleep.
items.you: Advise turning off the phone before bed.
items.app_line: I cannot sleep at night these days.
items.model_response: You should turn off your phone before you go to bed.

items.setup: A friend asks how you feel today.
items.you: Say you are much better than yesterday.
items.app_line: How are you feeling today?
items.model_response: Much better than yesterday, thank you for asking.

items.setup: A colleague asks what you think about working from home.
items.you: Give your opinion and one reason.
items.app_line: So, do you think working from home is a good idea?
items.model_response: I think it is a good idea because it saves time on travelling.

items.setup: A friend asks if you agree that breakfast is important.
items.you: Agree and give a short reason.
items.app_line: Do you agree that breakfast is the most important meal?
items.model_response: Yes, I agree, because it gives you energy for the whole morning.

items.setup: Someone says cities are better than the countryside.
items.you: Disagree politely and say why.
items.app_line: I honestly think cities are better than the countryside.
items.model_response: I am not sure I agree. In the countryside the air is cleaner and it is quieter.

items.setup: Your friend asks which language you find easiest to learn.
items.you: Say which and justify your choice.
items.app_line: Which language do you think is the easiest to learn?
items.model_response: I think English is the easiest for me because I hear it everywhere.

items.setup: A friend asks what you think of online shopping.
items.you: Say it is convenient but can be expensive.
items.app_line: What do you think about online shopping?
items.model_response: It is very convenient, but I think you can spend too much money easily.

items.setup: Your family argues about watching TV at dinner.
items.you: Say you think dinner should be without screens.
items.app_line: But dinner is so boring without the TV!
items.model_response: I think we should eat without screens so we can talk to each other.

items.setup: A classmate thinks money makes people happy.
items.you: Partially agree and add your own view.
items.app_line: I believe money is the key to happiness.
items.model_response: Money helps, of course, but I think friends and health matter more.

items.setup: A friend asks about a place that surprised you.
items.you: Describe a visit and what surprised you.
items.app_line: Tell me about a place that really surprised you.
items.model_response: I visited Valencia last year and I was surprised by how beautiful the city was.

items.setup: A colleague asks about a mistake you learned from.
items.you: Narrate briefly what happened and the lesson.
items.app_line: Have you ever made a mistake you learned a lot from?
items.model_response: Once I forgot an important appointment. Now I always check my calendar twice.

items.setup: A friend asks about the best meal you ever had.
items.you: Describe the meal and the occasion.
items.app_line: What is the best meal you have ever had?
items.model_response: The best meal I ever had was fresh seafood on holiday in Galicia.

items.setup: Your teacher asks about a challenge you overcame.
items.you: Explain the challenge and how you solved it.
items.app_line: Can you tell us about a challenge you overcame?
items.model_response: I was afraid of speaking in public, so I joined a club to practise and now I enjoy it.

items.setup: A friend asks if you have ever lived abroad.
items.you: Say whether you have and describe the experience briefly.
items.app_line: Have you ever lived in another country?
items.model_response: Yes, I lived in Ireland for six months and it was a fantastic experience.

items.setup: Your flatmate asks how you met your best friend.
items.you: Tell the story briefly.
items.app_line: How did you and your best friend meet?
items.model_response: We met at university during our first class and we sat next to each other.

items.setup: A friend asks about a concert or event you attended.
items.you: Describe it and how you felt.
items.app_line: Did you go to the concert last month?
items.model_response: Yes, I did. The atmosphere was amazing and I sang the whole night.

items.setup: An interviewer asks where you see yourself in five years.
items.you: Say you want to grow in your profession.
items.app_line: Where do you see yourself in five years?
items.model_response: I see myself growing in this profession and leading my own projects.

items.setup: Your friend asks what job you dream about.
items.you: Describe your dream job and why.
items.app_line: If you could do any job, what would it be?
items.model_response: I would love to be a travel photographer because I could see the world.

items.setup: Your manager asks if you can finish a report by Friday.
items.you: Accept and mention a plan to do it.
items.app_line: Could you have the report ready by Friday?
items.model_response: Yes, I can. I will finish the analysis tomorrow and write it on Thursday.

items.setup: A friend asks if you are going to do a course this year.
items.you: Say you are planning to study English abroad.
items.app_line: Do you have any plans for a course this year?
items.model_response: I am planning to study English abroad next summer.

items.setup: Your colleague worries about an important presentation.
items.you: Reassure them and offer to help.
items.app_line: I am so nervous about tomorrow's presentation.
items.model_response: Do not worry, you know the topic very well. I can help you rehearse if you want.

items.setup: A friend asks whether you would accept a job far from home.
items.you: Give your opinion with a condition.
items.app_line: Would you take a good job far from your city?
items.model_response: I would accept it if the salary and the conditions were really good.

items.setup: Your manager suggests an early meeting tomorrow.
items.you: Agree and confirm the time.
items.app_line: Shall we have the meeting at eight tomorrow?
items.model_response: That works for me. I will see you at eight then.

items.setup: You and a friend cannot decide what to do tonight.
items.you: Suggest going to the new cinema.
items.app_line: What shall we do tonight?
items.model_response: Why do not we go to the new cinema in the centre?

items.setup: Your team wants a cheaper team-building activity.
items.you: Suggest a picnic in the park.
items.app_line: Do you have any ideas for the team activity?
items.model_response: We could have a picnic in the park, it is cheap and fun.

items.setup: A friend wants to improve her English.
items.you: Suggest watching series with subtitles.
items.app_line: How can I improve my English quickly?
items.model_response: I suggest you watch series in English with English subtitles.

items.setup: Your partner wants a quick dinner.
items.you: Suggest making pasta together.
items.app_line: I do not want to cook anything complicated tonight.
items.model_response: Let us make pasta, it is quick and easy.

items.setup: A friend asks for a good way to relax.
items.you: Suggest doing yoga or going for a walk.
items.app_line: What do you do when you need to relax?
items.model_response: You should try yoga, or simply go for a long walk in the park.

items.setup: You want to surprise a friend for her birthday.
items.you: Suggest organising a small party.
items.app_line: How should we celebrate Ana's birthday?
items.model_response: Why do not we organise a small party at my place?

items.setup: Your group needs to decide where to study for exams.
items.you: Suggest the library because it is quiet.
items.app_line: Where shall we study this weekend?
items.model_response: How about the library? It is quiet and we can concentrate.

items.setup: A colleague argues that social media does more harm than good.
items.you: Argue the opposite side with two clear points.
items.app_line: I am convinced that social media has a negative effect on society.
items.model_response: I would argue it depends on how you use it. It connects people and gives small businesses a voice.

items.setup: Your friend thinks exams are the best way to assess students.
items.you: Challenge that idea and propose an alternative.
items.app_line: Exams are the only fair way to assess what students know.
items.model_response: I see your point, but exams only measure memory under pressure. Continuous projects show real understanding.

items.setup: A debate about electric cars is happening at work.
items.you: Present the case for electric cars with evidence.
items.app_line: Electric cars are still not a real solution.
items.model_response: They are not perfect, but they reduce emissions in cities and the technology improves every year.

items.setup: A friend claims that money can buy happiness.
items.you: Counter with psychological research or experience.
items.app_line: In my experience, money really does buy happiness.
items.model_response: Studies show that after a certain point, more money does not make people happier. Experiences and relationships do.

items.setup: Your manager wants to ban remote work.
items.you: Disagree and give reasons based on productivity.
items.app_line: I think we should all come back to the office full-time.
items.model_response: I respectfully disagree. Many of us are more productive at home, and flexibility reduces staff turnover.

items.setup: A relative thinks tourism ruins local culture.
items.you: Argue that tourism can also preserve culture.
items.app_line: Tourism only destroys local traditions.
items.model_response: That is true in some cases, but tourism can also fund the preservation of traditions and create jobs that keep communities alive.

items.setup: A debate about homework for young children.
items.you: Argue that young children should not have homework.
items.app_line: Children need homework from an early age to build discipline.
items.model_response: At a young age, play is how children learn best. Homework can wait until secondary school.

items.setup: Someone says reading is obsolete in the digital age.
items.you: Defend reading with strong arguments.
items.app_line: Who reads books anymore? Everything is online now.
items.model_response: Reading is far from obsolete. It develops deep thinking that short videos simply cannot provide.

items.setup: A friend wonders what you would change in your town.
items.you: Explain the change you would make and why.
items.app_line: If you could change one thing in our town, what would it be?
items.model_response: If I could change one thing, I would build more cycle lanes, because the traffic is getting worse every year.

items.setup: A colleague asks what you would do with a year off.
items.you: Describe your ideal plan for the year.
items.app_line: If you had a year off with money, what would you do?
items.model_response: I would travel across Asia for a few months and then volunteer teaching English somewhere.

items.setup: Your friend asks how your life would be different without the internet.
items.you: Speculate about the main differences.
items.app_line: Imagine life without the internet. How would yours change?
items.model_response: Without the internet, I would probably meet friends more often, but studying languages would be much harder.

items.setup: A friend says she would never live in a big city.
items.you: Explain under what conditions you would live in one.
items.app_line: I could never live in a huge city like London.
items.model_response: I would live in a big city if my job required it, but I would choose a quiet neighbourhood.

items.setup: Your teacher asks how you would handle a difficult client.
items.you: Explain your strategy calmly.
items.app_line: How would you deal with a client who is never satisfied?
items.model_response: I would listen carefully, take notes, and then propose a clear plan to solve each issue step by step.

items.setup: A friend wonders what you would take to a desert island.
items.you: Choose one object and justify it.
items.app_line: If you were alone on an island, what one object would you take?
items.model_response: I would take a solar-powered radio, because staying informed and connected would keep me sane.

items.setup: A meeting is deciding the launch date for a product.
items.you: Propose a realistic date and justify it.
items.app_line: When should we launch the new version?
items.model_response: I would suggest launching in early March. That gives us time to test everything properly before summer.

items.setup: Your team is choosing a new software tool.
items.you: Recommend one option and compare it briefly.
items.app_line: Which tool do you recommend for our team?
items.model_response: I recommend Tool A. It has better reporting and the team already knows its interface, so training would be faster.

items.setup: A colleague suggests cutting the feedback meeting.
items.you: Argue for keeping it with a shorter format.
items.app_line: I think we can skip the weekly feedback meeting.
items.model_response: I understand, but feedback keeps us aligned. We could shorten it to fifteen minutes instead of cancelling it.

items.setup: Your manager asks your opinion on a risky investment.
items.you: Express measured concern and suggest a safer route.
items.app_line: I am thinking of investing heavily in that start-up. What is your view?
items.model_response: I would be cautious. The idea is promising, but I would start with a smaller amount until they prove the model.

items.setup: A teammate missed a deadline and is making excuses.
items.you: Address the issue directly but constructively.
items.app_line: Sorry the report is late, I had a lot on my plate.
items.model_response: I understand you are busy, but the deadline matters. Next time, let us know earlier so we can redistribute the work.

items.setup: The team cannot agree on who leads the new project.
items.you: Propose a fair solution.
items.app_line: We cannot agree on a project leader.
items.model_response: Why do not we rotate the leadership each phase? That way everyone contributes and no one is overloaded.

items.setup: A client asks you to work at the weekend.
items.you: Decline politely and offer an alternative.
items.app_line: Could you finish this by Monday morning? It would mean working this weekend.
items.model_response: I am afraid I cannot work this weekend, but I can deliver it first thing Tuesday if that helps.

items.setup: A junior asks for feedback on her presentation.
items.you: Give balanced, specific feedback.
items.app_line: Could you give me some honest feedback on my presentation?
items.model_response: Your content was excellent. I would just slow down a little and make more eye contact with the audience.

items.setup: A seminar discusses whether AI will reduce human creativity.
items.you: Develop a nuanced position on the question.
items.app_line: Some argue that AI will make human creativity irrelevant.
items.model_response: I would argue the opposite: AI automates the routine parts, which actually frees people to focus on genuinely original thinking.

items.setup: A colleague questions the value of philosophy in modern education.
items.you: Defend its relevance with an abstract argument.
items.app_line: Honestly, philosophy has little practical value these days.
items.model_response: On the contrary, philosophy trains exactly the critical thinking that an automated world demands more than ever.

items.setup: In a debate about globalisation, you are asked to take a side.
items.you: Weigh benefits and drawbacks with precision.
items.app_line: Do you believe globalisation has ultimately done more harm than good?
items.model_response: It is a mixed picture. Globalisation has lifted millions out of poverty, yet it has also concentrated wealth and eroded local industries.

items.setup: Someone claims happiness is a choice.
items.you: Complicate that claim with nuance.
items.app_line: I believe happiness is simply a matter of choice.
items.model_response: That is only partially true. Attitude plays a role, but circumstances such as health and security are not simply matters of willpower.

items.setup: A friend believes cities should ban private cars completely.
items.you: Respond with a sophisticated counter-argument.
items.app_line: The only real solution is banning private cars from cities entirely.
items.model_response: A total ban would be disruptive without solving accessibility. A more effective approach combines congestion charges with radically better public transport.

items.setup: The conversation turns to whether failure builds character.
items.you: Reflect on the idea with a balanced view.
items.app_line: Do you think failure really builds character?
items.model_response: It can, provided there is time to reflect on it. Unprocessed failure tends to breed fear rather than resilience.

items.setup: A colleague argues that data always tells the truth.
items.you: Challenge the assumption about data.
items.app_line: The numbers never lie, that is why I trust data.
items.model_response: Numbers do not lie, but interpretations frequently do. The choice of metrics and framing shapes what the data appears to say.

items.setup: You are asked whether art should always be beautiful.
items.you: Articulate a considered opinion.
items.app_line: Do you think art should always be beautiful?
items.model_response: I would say art should be meaningful rather than beautiful. Some of the most powerful works are deliberately unsettling.

items.setup: Your manager proposes an idea you have reservations about.
items.you: Express measured disagreement politely.
items.app_line: So we are all agreed on moving the team overseas?
items.model_response: I would tend to agree with the overall direction, though I do have some reservations about the timing and the cost of relocation.

items.setup: A friend asks whether you think their plan will succeed.
items.you: Answer honestly with careful hedging.
items.app_line: So you think my business plan will actually work?
items.model_response: I think it stands a reasonable chance, provided the market research is as solid as you suggest, but nothing is guaranteed.

items.setup: Someone makes a strong claim about a politician.
items.you: Respond without taking an absolute position.
items.app_line: That politician is completely incompetent, everybody knows that.
items.model_response: I would be careful about sweeping judgements. Some of their policies are questionable, but they have also delivered on a few promises.

items.setup: A client is over-optimistic about delivery times.
items.you: Set expectations realistically without sounding negative.
items.app_line: I expect the full project in three weeks, as we discussed.
items.model_response: I am afraid three weeks is somewhat optimistic. Realistically, with testing, we are looking at closer to five.

items.setup: A friend claims their new diet is perfect.
items.you: Acknowledge the benefits but add nuance.
items.app_line: This diet is perfect, I have never felt better.
items.model_response: It clearly suits you, and that is great, though what works for one person does not always translate to another.

items.setup: A colleague asserts that their approach is the only valid one.
items.you: Suggest openness to alternatives diplomatically.
items.app_line: My method is the only one that gets real results.
items.model_response: Your results certainly speak for themselves, although I wonder whether other approaches might work just as well in different contexts.

items.setup: A friend asks for your honest view of their new partner.
items.you: Give a diplomatic yet sincere answer.
items.app_line: So what do you really think of my new partner?
items.model_response: They seem warm and genuinely good for you. I was a little unsure at first, but first impressions can be misleading.

items.setup: Your team debates whether to adopt a risky new technology.
items.you: Give a balanced recommendation with conditions.
items.app_line: Should we adopt the new system now or wait?
items.model_response: I would lean towards adopting it, but only after a controlled pilot, because the potential upside is high and the risk is manageable.

items.setup: A sponsor is hesitating to renew their funding.
items.you: Persuade them subtly by reframing the value.
items.app_line: I am still not convinced the sponsorship is worth renewing.
items.model_response: I understand the hesitation, yet the visibility your brand gains here reaches precisely the audience your campaign has struggled to capture elsewhere.

items.setup: A reluctant friend needs convincing to join your project.
items.you: Persuade them by appealing to shared ambitions.
items.app_line: I am not sure this project is for me.
items.model_response: Perhaps, but it offers exactly the challenge you have been telling me you want, and you would be leading it, not following.

items.setup: A client wants a discount you cannot offer.
items.you: Decline while preserving the relationship and future business.
items.app_line: Unless you can match that price, we will have to look elsewhere.
items.model_response: I completely respect that, and I would hate to lose you over a few points. What I can offer instead is a longer support term that will save you more in the long run.

items.setup: Your team resists a change you believe is essential.
items.you: Win them over by acknowledging the cost first.
items.app_line: We have heard change proposals before, and nothing ever improved.
items.model_response: You are right to be sceptical, and I will not pretend this is painless. What has changed is the market, and our option is to adapt deliberately or react chaotically later.

items.setup: A talented colleague wants to resign.
items.you: Persuade them to stay without applying pressure.
items.app_line: I have decided to hand in my resignation.
items.model_response: That is a significant decision. Before you do, tell me what would need to change here for you to reconsider, because losing you would be our loss, not yours.

items.setup: A neighbour opposes a community project you lead.
items.you: Turn their objection into an asset.
items.app_line: This project will only bring noise and strangers to our street.
items.model_response: I can see why that worries you. Ironically, the project includes the noise barrier and the community space that would give neighbours more say over who uses the street.

items.setup: A committee is split on your proposal.
items.you: Build consensus by finding common ground.
items.app_line: Half of us support your proposal, the other half strongly opposes it.
items.model_response: That divide tells me the proposal is touching something real. Perhaps we can agree on a trial period with clear review criteria, which gives both sides evidence rather than assumptions.

items.setup: An international partner misunderstands your position.
items.you: Clarify your view without causing offence.
items.app_line: So your company is simply refusing to cooperate with us.
items.model_response: I apologise if that is how it came across. Our position is the opposite: we are eager to cooperate, though we must first align on the regulatory constraints.

items.setup: A colleague takes credit for your work in a meeting.
items.you: Reclaim credit diplomatically in front of the group.
items.app_line: And I led the analysis that produced these results.
items.model_response: I am glad the analysis is valued. To be precise about the record, the methodology was developed jointly, and I handled the data modelling phase.

items.setup: A partner demands an unreasonable concession.
items.you: Refuse while keeping negotiations constructive.
items.app_line: We expect full ownership of the intellectual property as a condition.
items.model_response: I appreciate the clarity of your position. That particular term is not something we can concede, though we remain open to a licensing arrangement that protects both parties.

items.setup: A dignitary asks an intrusive personal question.
items.you: Deflect with grace while keeping the conversation warm.
items.app_line: Tell me, how much do you earn in your position?
items.model_response: I tend to keep such figures private, but I can tell you the role is both demanding and deeply rewarding, which is what I value most.

items.setup: Your counterpart makes an accusation based on a rumour.
items.you: Address it with composure and evidence.
items.app_line: We have heard you are planning to poach our clients.
items.model_response: That rumour is simply unfounded. Our policy is strictly non-solicitation, and I would welcome the chance to address any specific concerns directly.

items.setup: A delicate negotiation has reached an impasse.
items.you: Suggest a face-saving path forward.
items.app_line: If you cannot improve your offer, there is nothing left to discuss.
items.model_response: I would rather not leave value on the table for either side. What if we pause the commercial terms and revisit them once the technical scope is settled?

items.setup: A junior employee criticises your decision publicly.
items.you: Respond in a way that preserves their dignity and your authority.
items.app_line: With respect, your decision seems unfair to the whole team.
items.model_response: I welcome the candour, and I would ask you to bring such concerns to me directly, where they will always receive a full hearing.
